stemMd: Why does the author mention disagreements among the footnotes?

options.label: A
options.textMd: To show that the novel does not merely transfer unquestioned authority from the main text to the margins.

options.label: B
options.textMd: To prove that footnotes cannot contain evidence.

options.label: C
options.textMd: To argue that readers should ignore the notes.

options.label: D
options.textMd: To establish that all the sources are equally persuasive.

options.label: E
options.textMd: To explain why the clerk stops reading documents.

explanationMd: If every note supplied final truth, the novel would simply replace one authority with another. Conflicting notes require evaluation and preserve the distinction between evidence and a complete authoritative narrative.

distractorRationale.b: Disagreement does not eliminate their evidential value.
distractorRationale.e: He continues to discover and revise.
distractorRationale.d: The passage does not rank them equally.
distractorRationale.c: Readers must assess rather than ignore them.
